scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all reach across the
data-center fabric -- pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable, though pc_0_0
can still ping its own gateway 10.0.0.1. The NOC adds that both
spine routers reported their BGP session toward leaf_router_0_0 going
down at the same moment, while the leaf's uplink interfaces still
show UP. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on leaf_router_0_0

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_0 is the top-of-rack leaf for pc_0_0
  (host subnet 10.0.0.0/24 on eth2). Its only fabric attachment is
  EBGP: neighbor 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0, AS 65100) on eth0 and
  neighbor 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1, AS 65101) on eth1. With bgpd
  dead the leaf stops learning 10.0.1.0/24 and stops advertising
  10.0.0.0/24, so pc_0_0 is isolated from the fabric even though every
  physical link is still UP.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on leaf_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- this lab
  keeps its config in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so a restart fully restores
  the BGP configuration and sessions.

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03 on this fabric): bgpd is killed
together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh
remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration is
missing/empty on leaf_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on leaf_router_0_0. Unlike the vtysh-configured
kath labs, this lab has a persistent /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart
brings bgpd back WITH its full BGP configuration; the sessions to both
spines re-establish and pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 again.
scoring_axes: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BGP daemon (bgpd) on leaf_router_0_0 has crashed and is no longer
running. This is the sole root cause of the fabric-wide reachability loss.

Affected component: The bgpd process within the FRR suite on leaf_router_0_0.

Mechanism: With bgpd dead, leaf_router_0_0 sent TCP FIN/RST to both of
its eBGP peers, causing both spine_router_0_0 (172.16.0.4) and
spine_router_0_1 (172.16.0.8) to drop their sessions simultaneously —
exactly matching the NOC report. The spines confirm this: both show the
leaf peer (172.16.0.5 / 172.16.0.9) in "Active" state, and
spine_router_0_0's neighbor detail records "Connections established 1;
dropped 1 / Peer closed the session." Without bgpd, leaf_router_0_0
stops advertising 10.0.0.0/24 into the fabric and stops receiving
10.0.1.0/24 from the spines. Its own RIB contains only three directly
connected prefixes; no BGP routes exist. The gateway (10.0.0.1) is
still reachable from pc_0_0 because the eth2 connected route survives
in zebra, but every attempt to reach 10.0.1.2 returns "Destination Net
Unreachable" from that same gateway.

Localization: leaf_router_0_0 exclusively. Its /etc/frr/daemons has
bgpd=yes and /etc/frr/frr.conf contains a complete, valid BGP
configuration (AS 65200, neighbors 172.16.0.4 / 172.16.0.8, network
10.0.0.0/24), but no bgpd process exists and watchfrr is also absent,
meaning there is no auto-restart guard in place.

Root cause: bgpd was killed on leaf_router_0_0 with watchfrr not
running to restart it.

Corrective fix: Restart the FRR service on leaf_router_0_0
(`service frr restart` or `systemctl restart frr`). This will relaunch
bgpd (and watchfrr), reload frr.conf, re-establish eBGP sessions to
both spines, and restore end-to-end fabric reachability within one BGP
keepalive cycle (~60 s).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly and repeatedly localizes the failure to leaf_router_0_0 as the affected device (bgpd on that router is stopped).
The report explicitly states that the bgpd process on leaf_router_0_0 has crashed/is not running and treats that as the root cause.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-fabric: notes the spines, the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 are healthy (their other sessions stay Established), so the fault is only on leaf_router_0_0
per_axis.rationale: The report localizes the fault to leaf_router_0_0 and notes the two spines’ peer states, but it does not explicitly state that the super-spine and leaf_router_0_1 (and other sessions on the spines) remain healthy/Established.
Recommends restarting the FRR service (service frr restart / systemctl restart frr) to relaunch bgpd and restore BGP sessions, which matches the expected fix.

The investigation log shows direct checks (bgpd absent, frr.conf present, daemons file, missing watchfrr, spine neighbor states, and connectivity failure) that support the agent's conclusion; a few specific mechanistic claims (explicit TCP FIN/RST, exact RIB contents) are asserted without direct log snippets but do not undermine the main diagnosis.
